sermon.title: Division Part 2
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In “Division Part 2,” Pastor David G. Kincer continues through 1 Corinthians 1–2 and says unity is found in the power of God and the Spirit, not in excellent speaking, intellect or a favorite minister. He tells of his own changed life at the altar, why he recommends the baptism of the Holy Ghost, and why God has no grandchildren. He says we need God every day and not only in an emergency, and that love is spelled T-I-M-E.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words, and a Whisper speech-to-text pass of the same audio, which added punctuation and filled words the captions dropped. Punctuation, paragraphing and obvious caption errors were cleaned; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. The video ends mid-sentence.

chunks.section_question: Why do people call the gospel foolishness?
chunks.short_answer: He says Jesus is a stumbling block to the Jews because they wanted a sign, and to the Gentiles it is “foolishness because they’re looking for total intellect,” just human reasoning rather than spiritual or scriptural reasoning. He says the preaching of Jesus Christ, the gospel and the cross is what saved him: “He died for me.”
chunks.text: So, where’s the power of God and the preaching of Jesus Christ, the Gospel, and the cross? And folks, that’s what saved me. He convicted me. He died for me. If he died for me to forgive me, then I owe him something. I have a debt to show my appreciation by what? Living for him. And if I fall, I get back up, admit it, and keep going. The Jews require a sign, and the Gentiles [unclear] intellect, and the Jews see Jesus as a stumbling block because they want a sign, and he didn’t give them any sign but the death and burial and resurrection. So Jesus is a stumbling block to the Jews who have their own opinion on how this is going to work out. And the Gentiles, it’s foolishness because they’re looking for total intellect, just total human reasoning, not spiritual reasoning, not scriptural reasoning, human reasoning. And so they go, oh, this is nonsense. How can anybody be born of a virgin? How can anybody, you know, be raised from the dead?

chunks.section_question: Should we look to ministers or to Jesus?
chunks.short_answer: He says Paul calls Jesus our wisdom, righteousness, sanctification and redemption, and the others were “nothing but messengers.” He says the American church looks to ministers and church groups instead of Christ, and people go to the church “where they’re comfortable, where their toes aren’t stepped on.” But you can go to a lousy church, look for Jesus, find him and be changed.
chunks.text:
This is foolishness. So you’ve got to have scriptural reasoning, spiritual reasoning. And then Paul says, Jesus is our wisdom, our righteousness, sanctification, our power, our redemption, and our glory, our honor. Do we agree with that? Yeah. So what does Paul have to do with it? What does Apollos and Priscilla and Peter, what do they have to do with it? Nothing but messengers, get out of the way, give me Jesus. And what is the American church looking to? The people, they’re looking to ministers. They’re looking to a church group. Instead of Christ and the power of the gospel, we’re looking to somebody. Even people will say, we need a leader to be raised up. We need Jesus to arise in our lives.

And people go to the church where they’re comfortable, where their toes aren’t stepped on, and, you know, they got the music and whatever. And, you know, they go and they leave the same way that they came. And that’s because that’s what Christians choose to do. You know, you can go to a lousy church and look for Jesus and find him and be changed because he will meet you no matter where you’re at. And you can wind up being a force in that church.

chunks.section_question: Does it take great speaking to change lives?
chunks.short_answer: He says unity is in the power of God and the Spirit, “not the excellent intellectual speaking.” Even Apollos, who could speak, lacked the fullness of the message until Priscilla and Aquila came along. The only demonstration of the Spirit and power we have seen so far, he says, is “salvation and changed lives.”
chunks.text:
Okay. I’m going to have to stop in the middle of this message because I don’t want to wear you out. We’re in a conference and we’ve got to have a break. Conferences have breaks. We can pick up this message next week. But unity, number four statement he makes, unity is in the power of God and the spirit, not the excellent intellectual speaking. It doesn’t matter if I went to college and learned how to speak intellectually and excellently. It doesn’t matter if I graduated from Toastmasters with the greatest honor and I can really speak. See, Apollos could speak. He had the Toastmasters ability to speak, but he lacked the fullness of the message till Priscilla and Aquila came along and enlarged his ability to speak the truth. He was limited in the truth he spoke.

“I declared not God’s mystery with excellent speech, but in weakness, in fear and much trembling. In demonstration of the spirit and power.” So far, the only demonstration of the spirit and power we’ve seen is salvation and changed lives. These people were holy. They were pursuing moral blamelessness. They were fellowshipping with Jesus. These people were very powerful. And so the demonstration of the power is what these Corinthians’ changed lives, from homosexuality, adultery, prostitution, slavery, slave masters, all this debauchery that was going on. The power he’s talking about is the changed life.

When I was young, they convinced me that we’re going to reach the world. We need miracles. And we need the [unclear]. My group had convinced me till God changed my thinking that we needed the gifts operating. But here in this church, we see the power of the spoken word, don’t we? And Christ backing up his word. Hallelujah.

scriptures.text_nkjv: And I, brethren, when I came to you, did not come with excellence of speech or of wisdom declaring to you the testimony of God. chunks.section_question: Can God really change a person?
chunks.short_answer: He says he went to the altar and “really experienced salvation,” then was baptized in water and “the presence of God came on me and it scared me to death.” After he was filled with the Holy Ghost, he says, he left church that night “in love with everybody.” He says “the power of God is real” and “we keep changing.”
chunks.text:
And that’s what changed me, folks. I went to that altar and I really experienced salvation. It was real. These people weren’t lying to me. Two weeks later or one week later, I got baptized in water and the presence of God came on me and it scared me to death. I had never felt anything like that before. My goodness, I did [unclear] because I was resisting.

What in the world is going on? One week after that or two weeks after [unclear], I was filled with the Holy Ghost with speaking in tongues because that’s what they emphasize. And, you know, when you experience these things, it’s real. The power of God is real. He backs up what he says. And I remember leaving the church that night in love with everybody. I didn’t have any enemies. That Holy Spirit just made me fall in love with Jesus and the church and everybody. A changed person. And we keep changing. When we keep pursuing, we keep what? Changing.

chunks.section_question: Why does he recommend the baptism of the Holy Ghost?
chunks.short_answer: He says your faith is “not in the wisdom of man, but in the power of God,” when the Spirit “ignites it in me and makes it real to me.” He highly recommends the baptism of the Holy Ghost and Spirit-filled churches “in spite of our problems and our extremism,” because they look for the presence of Christ, which can change you if you let it.
chunks.text: Number four is repeated again in this verse. Your faith is not in the wisdom of man, but in the power of God. What the Holy Spirit teaches. What what teaches? The Holy Spirit. So it’s not what Schuller [unclear] says. It’s not what [unclear] or Robert[unclear] says or Billy Graham says. It’s what they say and the Spirit ignites it in me and makes it real to me. That’s when I hear. That Holy Spirit is important. I keep telling you, I highly recommend the baptism of the Holy Ghost. I highly recommend the Spirit filled churches in spite of our problems and our extremism and all the rest. I highly recommend them because on a consistent basis, they’re looking for the presence of Christ, the presence of the Holy Spirit, which can change you if you let it, or it can just be an emotional experience that, you know, you don’t, you don’t change.

chunks.section_question: What is the difference between feeling God’s presence and being filled with the Holy Ghost?
chunks.short_answer: He tells of a priest who said he was filled with the Holy Ghost, and says he told him “you experienced the presence of God,” but the Holy Ghost “comes within you and pours out of you. There’s a big difference.” We need to be filled, controlled and influenced by it from within, he says, and with that power “I don’t have to disfellowship people” because “I know who I am.”
chunks.text:
I told you before, I met a priest that said he was, in fact, I invited him to speak in the church. He said he was filled with the Holy Ghost and preached a good message. After the service, I was talking to him, he used profanity, he lit up a cigarette, and I go, sir, do you know the first name of the Spirit? He looks at me. What? The first name of the Spirit, first name of the Ghost. What is it? Holy. I go, yeah. How can you talk like that? How can you do these things? I said, tell me exactly how you got filled with the Holy Ghost. He said, well, I went down to the Anaheim Convention Center and there’s 10,000 Catholics in there. You know, there’s charismatic Catholics, you know, worshiping God and the presence of God was there. I go, yes, that’s exactly it. You experienced the presence of God. The Holy Ghost comes within you and pours out of you. There’s a big difference. Can I hear an amen?

I said, you haven’t been filled with the Holy Ghost. And he’s looking at me, but he knew I was right. He experienced the presence of the Spirit, but we need to be what? Filled with it, controlled by it, influenced by it. From within, it needs to come out from within. It’s powerful, church. I tell you, that’s where you get power to think right, and act right and get up from your stupid actions and repent, really, and get in control of your life. That Holy Ghost drives you to be like Jesus and empowers you to do it. And so Paul is telling us what? Unity should be around the power, whether it’s Christ, whether it’s his gospel, whether it’s his death, burial and resurrection. It should be in the power, not in intellectual thinking and opinions. If the power is not working in my life, I’m missing it.

And see, when I have the power, I don’t have to disfellowship people. I know who I am. I know where I’m going. They can talk about me. They can belittle me. They can be in a total different camp than I am at, and it doesn’t affect me. Why? Because I have power. I know who I am. I know who Christ is. And I know I was where they were at at one time. Are you there? I was just like them at one time. And Christ kept changing me.

chunks.section_question: Should you read the Bible with your mind or with the Holy Spirit?
chunks.short_answer: He says the Holy Spirit “is what opens the Scriptures to you,” so when you read and study you should “lean on that Holy Spirit, not your mental intellect.” He says he has to make a transition from his natural mind to the mind of the Spirit, and that Jesus and the Holy Spirit are each a separate work in your life “and yet they’re all the same.”
chunks.text:
The Holy Spirit, the Bible says is what opens the Scriptures to you. And when you read it and study it, you need to lean on that Holy Spirit, not your mental intellect. The natural man receives not the things of the Spirit, but he that is spiritual, judges, determines, examines all things. See, Dave Kincer has to make a transition from his natural mind to the mind of the Spirit, from his natural person to the person of the Spirit, Jesus. You can’t separate the Holy Ghost from Jesus. They’re separated in the Bible so that we understand more and all that. And the Trinity really explains it.

But just knowing the word Trinity doesn’t work. See, Jesus is a separate work in your life. And the Holy Spirit is a separate work in your life. And yet they’re all the same. You say, how can that be? He is God. He’s supernatural.

chunks.section_question: Why does he say Paul has more credibility than modern authors?
chunks.short_answer: He says Paul got saved five years after Christ ascended, wrote his epistles less than twenty years after, and mingled with Peter, John and Luke. “He’s got more credibility than any of these book authors,” he says, and more than any church growth seminar. Paul “used nothing but the scriptures and reasoning,” and then Christ backed it up.
chunks.text:
And so we’ve got eight more points that Paul is going to bring out. And I’m purposely stopping because we need to get this stuff. And we can continue next week. But this is the Apostle Paul talking. This is a guy that got saved five years after Christ died on the cross and ascended.

This is a guy that wrote these epistles just less than 20 years after Christ ascended. This is the guy that mingled with Paul, I mean with Peter and John and Luke and these guys that were with Christ. And I submit to you, he’s got more credibility than any of these book authors. He’s got more credibility than any of these church growth seminars you can go to. That’s why I said we’re at a church growth seminar conference. How to start a church, how to develop a church and how to govern a church. Because we need to get this stuff in us.

And he used nothing but the scriptures and reasoning to get this done. And then Christ came in and backed it up. And he’s trying to get them to focus on the power, not people, not ministers, not a group.

chunks.section_question: Can your church, your denomination or a minister save you?
chunks.short_answer: He says the problem in America is “my granddad was a Baptist and my dad was a Baptist and I’m a Baptist, don’t bug me,” and the same with Catholics. Catholics, Baptists, Pentecostals and Jews “can’t save you,” he says, but “Jesus Christ can.” He says to put your confidence on Jesus and the gospel, because “you cannot undermine the power of the cross.”
chunks.text:
The problem in America is if my granddad was a Baptist and my dad was a Baptist and I’m a Baptist, don’t bug me. If my granddad was a Catholic and my dad was a Catholic and I’m a Catholic, don’t bug me. No, you don’t focus. Catholics can’t save you, Baptists can’t save you, Pentecostals can’t save you, Jews can’t save you, they can’t change you, Jesus Christ can. You need to get your confidence out of that group and onto Jesus and the gospel and that’s a good place for an amen. You need to get your confidence in these ministers, [unclear], Jakes and [unclear] and [unclear] and all these people and get your confidence on who? Jesus Christ. You need to be seekers, not of ministers and a church group, you need to be seekers of who? Jesus and his gospel and that cross.

Everywhere I go I tell people you cannot undermine the power of the cross, the death of Christ. There’s no sin, it can’t forgive. There’s no Christian that backslid that he can’t restore. There’s such power in the cross that I never got saved again. I kept getting changed. I kept getting corrected but I never answered another salvation altar call. Hallelujah.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Jesus answered and said to him, “Most assuredly, I say to you, unless one is born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God.”

chunks.short_answer: He says that after 9/11 the churches filled with people praying, but within 60 days they were empty again, because people “think God is only good for an immediate necessity.” In his own emergency, he says, he had already put in his prayer time, and he did not need “a healer to come in here. I need the healer. Jesus.”
chunks.text:
And then we want God. 9/11 came and the churches were filled with people praying. See, that’s how quickly God can change things. But did it last? No. 60 days. Churches were empty again. Why? They think God is only good for an immediate necessity. And that God will be there at the snap of their finger. And they are totally wrong. We need him every day of our life. You see.

I had a tragic come in my life and somebody says, man, you know, do you pray and what do you do? I said, I just do what I always do. I just live my life. I’ve already put in my prayer time for this emergency. I don’t need to call no 24 heartline. I don’t need to get frustrated. I don’t need to get depressed. I have done what I’m supposed to do. And all I got to do is just keep doing it. When I was dying in that hospital, they’d ask me these things. And I go, you know, I don’t need a healer to come in here. I need the healer. Jesus.

I’m not panicked. Why, I’ve done what I was supposed to do. And I’m in his hands. He makes the decisions. I don’t have to get holy water or some magical formula. You know, people tried to get me to get into this magical formula for healing. I said, ain’t no magical formula for healing. He either heals you, or he doesn’t. He’s the healer. You ask him, he responds, or you die. We all got to die. Well, aren’t you depressed? Aren’t you worried? What am I going to [unclear]? Either I die today or would have died 20 years from now. paragraphs.text: And then we want God. 9/11 came and the churches were filled with people praying. See, that’s how quickly God can change things. But did it last? No. 60 days. Churches were empty again. Why? They think God is only good for an immediate necessity. And that God will be there at the snap of their finger. And they are totally wrong. We need him every day of our life. You see.

I had a tragic come in my life and somebody says, man, you know, do you pray and what do you do? I said, I just do what I always do. I just live my life. chunks.section_question: Can you call on God and expect him to come?
chunks.short_answer: He says we shouldn’t settle for a service or a prayer time without him, and should say, “you said if I drew nigh to you, you’d draw nigh to me.” He says God is “more than glad to respond to the summons,” though “he doesn’t come except in his sovereign times.” He adds that when God summons us to assemble, pray and seek his word, we have to put it in our schedule.
chunks.text:
But see, that’s what the Holy Ghost and the Word will do for you. And I’m sharing that with you. That’s the power. When you need it, it’s there. It’s there because you’ve been there. Now, how many could use a little holiness in your life? A little sainthood in your life where you are striving for moral blamelessness? A little fellowship with Jesus daily? Yeah. A little summoning Christ. Quit calling on him. But saying, hey, bud, you said you would come. I’m summoning you. I’m serving you papers. Get here. We need you. Without you, we’re nothing.

And not settle for a service that doesn’t have him. Or a prayer time when you go in your closet at home. Don’t settle for him not coming. Say, hey, boy, you said if I drew nigh to you, you’d draw nigh to me. You said if I come to church and assembled, you would be there. We summon you. And he’s what? More than glad to respond to the summons. But when you just go, Jesus, would you please come? Jesus, we love you. Jesus, help me. You know, we don’t expect him to come. We don’t demand him to come. He doesn’t come except in his sovereign times.

Hallelujah. But when you’re summoned, you never miss it, do you? You know the penalty of not answering a summons. Well, maybe you haven’t been summoned. I’ve been summoned. Let me tell you, it’s not fun getting that paper. I know I got to put it in my schedule. And how many of you know he’s summoning you to assemble together? And you got to put it in your schedule. Wow, that’s hot stuff. He’s summoning you for a prayer time. And you got to put it in your schedule. He’s summoning you to seek his word. And you got to put it into your schedule. If you want him to respond when you want him to respond, then you ought to back it up by what? You’re responding when he wants you to respond. Now that’s good stuff.

chunks.section_question: Do we need the power of God, or just the motions?
chunks.short_answer: He asks how many of us need to be speaking the same thing, with no division and making right judgments. He asks how many need to “possess the power” and not just lean on messages we have heard: “we just go through the motions when we need the power.”
chunks.text: Hallelujah. How many of us need to be speaking the same thing? And no division. Making right judgments. See, how many of us need to possess the power? And not just lean on, well, I’ve heard Moses’ tabernacle. I’ve heard David’s tabernacle. I’ve heard the cross message. And we just go through the motions when we need the power.

And not just lean on, well, I’ve heard Moses’ tabernacle. I’ve heard David’s tabernacle. I’ve heard the cross message. And we just go through the motions when we need the power.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Now I plead with you, brethren, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions among you, but that you be perfectly joined together in the same mind and in the same judgment.

chunks.short_answer: He says you won’t get the power watching TV, and sports and recreation don’t give it either: he finds it “spending time with the sources of power.” Love, he says, is not only spelled L-O-V-E, “it’s spelled T-I-M-E,” and if he says he loves God he will spend time with him. He adds that he cannot separate love for Christ from love for his people.

faqs.question: Why did he stop in the middle of the message?
faqs.answer: He says he doesn’t want to wear them out: they are in a conference, and conferences have breaks. He says they can pick up the message next week, and that Paul has eight more points to bring out.

faqs.question: Who was Apollos, according to this message?
faqs.answer: He says Apollos could speak and “had the Toastmasters ability to speak,” but he lacked the fullness of the message until Priscilla and Aquila came along and enlarged his ability to speak the truth. “He was limited in the truth he spoke.”

faqs.question: What kind of changed lives did Paul’s preaching bring about in Corinth?
faqs.answer: He says the power Paul talks about is the changed life. These people were pursuing moral blamelessness and fellowshipping with Jesus, and he says the Corinthians’ lives were changed from homosexuality, adultery, prostitution, slavery, slave masters and all the debauchery that was going on.

scriptures.text_nkjv: And I, brethren, when I came to you, did not come with excellence of speech or of wisdom declaring to you the testimony of God. For I determined not to know anything among you except Jesus Christ and Him crucified. I was with you in weakness, in fear, and in much trembling. And my speech and my preaching were not with persuasive words of human wisdom, but in demonstration of the Spirit and of power, that your faith should not be in the wisdom of men but in the power of God.

faqs.question: Is being filled with the Spirit just an emotional experience?
faqs.answer: He says the presence of Christ and of the Holy Spirit can change you if you let it, “or it can just be an emotional experience that, you know, you don’t, you don’t change.”

faqs.question: What does he say the Holy Ghost does for you?
faqs.answer: He says that is where you get power to think right and act right, to repent and get in control of your life. “That Holy Ghost drives you to be like Jesus and empowers you to do it.”

faqs.question: Does having God’s power mean you have to cut people off?
faqs.answer: He says no: “when I have the power, I don’t have to disfellowship people. I know who I am.” People can talk about him or belittle him, he says, and it doesn’t affect him, because he has power and knows who Christ is.

faqs.question: What does he say we should be seekers of?
faqs.answer: He says we should be seekers not of ministers and a church group but of “Jesus and his gospel and that cross.”

faqs.question: Is there any sin the cross can’t forgive?
faqs.answer: He says you cannot undermine the power of the cross, the death of Christ: “There’s no sin, it can’t forgive.” He also says there is no Christian who backslid that he can’t restore, and that he himself never got saved again but kept getting changed and corrected.

faqs.question: Is division a big problem in America?
faqs.answer: He says yes, and that we are losing the battle, and one of the main reasons is the church is so divided. He says we are preaching our own opinions and acting the way we want.

faqs.question: What does he say he did when a tragedy came?
faqs.answer: He says he did what he always does: he lived his life, because he had already put in his prayer time for the emergency. He didn’t need to get frustrated or depressed, he says, because all he had to do was keep doing what he was supposed to do.

faqs.question: Does he say there is a magical formula for healing?
faqs.answer: He says he doesn’t have to get holy water or some magical formula. People tried to get him into a magical formula for healing, he says, and he told them there is none: “He either heals you, or he doesn’t. He’s the healer.”

faqs.question: Why does he compare God’s call to a summons?
faqs.answer: He says when you are summoned, “you never miss it,” and you put it in your schedule. He says God is summoning us to assemble together, to pray and to seek his word, and if we want him to respond when we want, we should respond when he wants.

faqs.question: Can you separate love for Christ from love for his people?
faqs.answer: He says he cannot separate love for Christ from love for his people. The video ends as he begins to say more about love.
